items.headline: Sensex falls 429 points to 72,638.70 and Nifty 0.76% to 22,603.05 after the RBI hike
items.summary: Ends a two-day rally. The auto index fell 1.6%, realty 1.8% and FMCG 0.9% as the RBI moved to 'calibrated tightening' and called the inflation outlook 'no longer benign'. Ongoing pressure.
items.rationale: Rate-sensitive sectors reprice for dearer loans and slower spending; a tighter stance keeps valuations under pressure while oil stays high.

items.headline: 10-year G-Sec yield settles at 7.24%, highest since December 2023, as traders price a December hike
items.summary: The yield closed up from 7.19% after touching 7.27%. A primary dealer called the policy tone hawkish and said a December hike is now seen as confirmed; outflows and oil added pressure. Escalating.
items.rationale: Higher government bond yields lift borrowing costs for companies and the state and cut the value of banks' bond holdings.

items.headline: Foreign investors sell ₹6,121 crore on hike day, a fourth straight session; domestic funds buy ₹4,597 crore
items.summary: Foreign selling roughly doubled from Tuesday's ₹2,961 crore while domestic institutions kept buying, but not enough to offset it. Escalating.
items.rationale: Heavier foreign selling weighs on large banks and index heavyweights and adds dollar demand that pressures the rupee.

items.headline: Brent climbs over 2% to about $102.50 as Iran steps up attacks on Hormuz tankers
items.summary: A dozen attacks hit between 28 September and 2 October; Tuesday's Hormuz flows were the lowest since late July. US Gulf producers are shutting in output ahead of a possible hurricane. Escalating, despite faster IEA stock releases.
items.rationale: Crude above $100 widens India's import bill, keeps fuel inflation and rupee pressure high, and squeezes airlines, paint and fuel retailers.

items.headline: Iran's Guard says Hormuz is closed; US Central Command calls it false and says 20 million barrels are moving
items.summary: An adviser to Iran's Revolutionary Guard commander said the strait is closed and other routes would soon be shut; a tanker was attacked off Qatar. Iran also cited a safe-route understanding with Oman. Escalating rhetoric.
items.rationale: Closure threats on the route that carries much of India's crude and LNG keep insurance, freight and price risk premiums high even while cargoes still move.

items.headline: India's Venezuelan crude imports set for about 465,000 barrels a day in October, highest since 2019
items.summary: Up from about 196,000 in September, according to ship-tracking estimates. The grade is sold at a discount while Russian barrels now carry a premium. New supply shift.
items.rationale: Cheaper non-Gulf barrels diversify supply away from Hormuz and help complex refiners' margins, trimming the import bill at the edge.

items.headline: US 10-year yield touches 5.35%, highest since 2002, as Fed minutes show officials expect more hikes
items.summary: The yield eased to about 5.29% after a solid auction. Futures price the Fed rate rising to about 4.1% by January. It is up 60 bps since July as US crude rose 20%. Escalating.
items.rationale: Higher US yields pull foreign money out of Indian stocks and bonds, push up the dollar and limit room for Indian rates to ease.

items.headline: IT services Q2 results season opens with previews pointing to flat to 2% quarterly growth
items.summary: Previews see large firms at -0.4% to +2.0% in constant currency, with soft deal wins and AI-driven pricing pressure; mid-sized firms are expected to do better. Results due through late October. New.
items.rationale: Muted growth and pricing pressure cap IT earnings, while the weak rupee adds a currency gain that cushions margins.

items.headline: India presses Russia and Ukraine to halt attacks on ships after more Indian crew are hurt in the Black Sea
items.summary: India condemned strikes on commercial vessels and is discussing safe passage with both sides; its truce plan covers energy sites, Black Sea shipping and grain exports. Drone strikes near Bulgaria sank a ship. Ongoing.
items.rationale: Black Sea attacks raise risk for Russian crude, fertiliser and edible-oil supply to India; a truce would ease those costs.
